speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent, and I see you have a skin condition on your left dorsal hand; how long have you noticed it, and does it hurt or itch?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of diabetes and sunbathing, have you noticed any specific changes in the skin texture, such as thickening, yellowing, or the appearance of new nodules or ulcers on your left hand?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. The description of a rough, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand of a sun-exposed individual with a history of sunbathing is classic for this premalignant skin lesion. No further tests or questions are required.
